pairs.subject: companion-runtime
pairs.evidence: src/components/dashboard/views/messages/useMessagesData.ts:51 Messages come from a read-only synced_messages table (or mock threads) and Settings only toggles preference stores, so this context hosts no companion runtime: no turns, model legs, action execution or background cycles. A case-insensitive grep of src/components/dashboard (which covers both view dirs and ThreadRow's dir) for runTurn, turnSink, actionCatalog, workingSet and systemPrompt found nothing; the only 'companion' hits are Athena spend charts in observability, outside this context.

techniques.evidence: src/components/dashboard/views/messages/messages-page/ThreadDetailModal.tsx:118 The thread modal only renders persisted message bodies. It has no compose box and runs no turns, so there is no turn stream to make headless.

src/components/dashboard/views/settings/settings-sections/ModelProvidersCard.tsx:24 The provider card is a demo-only allowlist toggle over mock providers. It makes no model call, so there is no leg to meter.
src/components/dashboard/views/messages/index.tsx:117 The only mutations here are user-driven read-state and settings toggles. No model emits action kinds, so there is no catalog to keep in parity.

src/components/dashboard/views/settings/settings-sections/NotificationsCard.tsx:78 These are consumer-side alert-severity preferences. The producer-side decision about whether a background outcome deserves attention (announce or absorb) is made outside this context, in the desktop app or orchestrator.
